<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Regem magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.

<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is a great King * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is a great King * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is a great King * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is a great King * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

<r>1 Reg 10:1-2</r>
<n>1</n> Tulit autem Sámuel lentículam ólei, et effúdit super caput ejus: et deosculátus est eum, et ait: Ecce unxit te Dóminus super hereditátem suam in príncipem, et liberábis pópulum suum de mánibus inimicórum ejus qui in circúitu ejus sunt. Et hoc tibi signum, quia unxit te Deus in príncipem.
<n>2</n> Cum abíeris hódie a me, invénies duos viros juxta sepúlcrum Rachel in fínibus Bénjamin, in merídie: dicéntque tibi: Invéntæ sunt ásinæ ad quas íeras perquiréndas: et intermíssis pater tuus ásinis, sollícitus est pro vobis, et dicit: Quid fáciam de fílio meo?

b.7be2b2f50a:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>T</c>értio Idus Iúnii Luna séptima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>O</h>ctáva sacratíssimi Cordis Jesu.
<h>S</h>alamínæ, in Cypro, natális sancti Bárnabæ Apóstoli, qui, natióne Cýprius, cum Paulo Géntium Apóstolus a discípulis ordinátus, multas regiónes cum eo peragrávit, iniúnctum sibi opus Evangélicæ prædicatiónis exércens; postrémo, Cyprum proféctus, ibi Apostolátum suum glorióso martýrio decorávit. Ejus corpus, témpore Zenónis Imperatóris, ipso Bárnaba revelánte, repértum est, una cum códice Evangélii sancti Matthǽi, ejúsdem Bárnabæ manu descrípto.
<h>S</h>almánticæ, in Hispánia, item natális sancti Joánnis a sancto Facúndo, ex Eremitárum sancti Augustíni Ordine, Confessóris; qui fídei zelo, sanctimónia vitæ ac miráculis cláruit. Ipsíus autem festívitas sequénti die celebrátur.
<h>A</h>quiléiæ pássio sanctórum Felícis et Fortunáti fratrum, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni et Maximiáni, equúleo suspénsi, atque, ardéntibus lampádibus circa eórum látera appósitis et mox divína virtúte exstínctis, per ventrem fervénti oleo sunt perfúsi; et ad últimum, cum in Christi confessióne persísterent, gloriósi certáminis cursum, obtruncáti cápite, implevérunt.
<h>B</h>remæ natális sancti Rembérti, Hamburgénsis ac Breménsis Epíscopi.
<h>T</h>arvísii sancti Parísii, civis Bononiénsis, Confessóris et Mónachi, ex Ordine Camaldulénsi.
<h>R</h>omæ Translátio sancti Gregórii Nazianzéni, Epíscopi, Confessóris atque Ecclésiæ Doctóris; cujus sacrum corpus, e Constantinópoli ántea delátum ad Urbem, atque in Ecclésia sanctæ Dei Genitrícis ad Campum Mártium diu asservátum, Gregórius Décimus tértius, Póntifex Máximus, in Capéllam, a se in Basílica sancti Petri magnificentíssime exornátam, summa celebritáte tránstulit, ac postrídie digno honóre sub altári cóndidit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.c208096e07:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>une 11th 2027, the 7th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>T</h>he Octave of the most Sacred Heart of Jesus.
<h>T</h>he holy Apostle Barnabas. He was a Cypriot by birth, was by the disciples ordained an Apostle to the Gentiles along with Paul, and went through many countries with him doing that work of preaching the Gospel which had been laid upon them. In the end he went home to Cyprus, where he crowned the dignity of the Apostolate with the glory of martyrdom. Through a revelation from himself his body was discovered in the time of the Emperor Zeno, having with it a copy of the Gospel according to Matthew written with his own hand.
<h>A</h>t Aquileia, the holy brethren Felix and Fortunatus, both martyrs. In the persecution under Diocletian and Maximian they were hung upon the rack, and lighted lamps put to their sides, but these were extinguished by the power of God. Boiling oil was poured into their bellies, and at last, forasmuch as they still stood firm in confessing Christ, they were beheaded.
<h>A</h>t Bologna, [in the year 1267,] the holy Confessor Parisius, a monk of the Order of Camaldoli.
<h>A</h>t Rome is commemorated the translation of the body of holy Gregory of Nazianzus. This sacred body had been brought to Rome from Constantinople and had lain for a long time in the church of the Mother of God at the Campus Martius, when the Supreme Pontiff Gregory XIII, [in the year 1580,] removed it with great pomp to the chapel which he had splendidly decorated in the Basilica of St Peter, and there laid it under the altar with due honour.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>P</c>rotéctor in te sperántium, Deus, sine quo nihil est válidum, nihil sanctum; multíplica super nos misericórdiam tuam; ut, te rectóre, te duce, sic transeámus per bona temporália, ut non amittámus ætérna.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.113b36730a:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, the protector of all them that trust in thee, without whom nothing is strong, nothing is holy; increase and multiply upon us thy mercy, that thou being our ruler and guide, we may so pass through things temporal, that we finally lose not the things eternal.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
